title: The Swindler and the Three Spice Merchants

keywords: tale of the chear and the merchants
full_text:
A smooth-tongued swindler arrived in the spice bazaar of Cairo, dressed in the luxurious brocades of an imperial merchant of Samarkand. He approached three prominent spice dealers, offering to purchase their entire inventory of cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg on credit, promising to pay thirty thousand dinars upon the arrival of his caravan next morning.

Two of the younger merchants were dazzled by the prospect of enormous profit, but the third, an experienced elder named Abu Bakr, noticed that the stranger’s hands were soft as a child’s, without the calluses of a merchant who managed camel caravans, and that his servants looked like hired street loafers.

Abu Bakr gathered his two colleagues in secret: 'Do not release a single ounce of spice on promises! Let us demand that he deposit a commercial bond in the guild treasury, as the law of Cairo requires.'

When the three merchants stood together and insisted on the lawful bond, the impostor began to bluster and threaten to take his business elsewhere.

Abu Bakr summoned the guild inspector, who checked the imperial merchant registry: the stranger’s name was completely unknown, and his 'caravan' was a phantom of air!

The exposed swindler was expelled from Cairo.

The three merchants embraced in mutual gratitude, having learned that collective guild solidarity and adherence to verified rules protect the community from the most glittering deceptions.
moral: Commercial solidarity and shared vigilance protect honest traders from fraudulent impostors.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
